commands.review_summary:
The PR changes the realtime voice consult speakable-result limiter to use `truncateUtf16Safe` and adds a surrogate-boundary regression test.

PR surface: Source +1, Tests +27. Total +28 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Current main is source-reproducible because the raw `slice(0, maxChars - 16)` path can cut between an emoji's UTF-16 surrogate halves when the cap is 24 for a seven-character prefix.

target.title: fix(talk): keep consult result truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted with Codex.
- Realtime voice consult speakable result truncation now preserves UTF-16 boundaries while keeping the existing marker.
- Replaces raw UTF-16 code-unit truncation with the existing UTF-16-safe truncation helper.
- Keeps the existing cap/truncation signal behavior; out of scope: unrelated slices and response-read bounding.

## Linked context

- No linked issue.
- Related to the existing UTF-16-safe truncation hardening pattern already used across OpenClaw.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Realtime voice consult speakable result truncation now preserves UTF-16 boundaries while keeping the existing marker.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on Node v22.22.0.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/talk/consult-question.test.ts
- Evidence after fix: focused test passed, 4 tests.
- Observed result after fix: the touched OpenClaw path no longer emits a lone surrogate when truncating text at an emoji boundary.
- What was not tested: full end-to-end provider/channel delivery was not run; this is a focused text-boundary fix.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: proof is scoped to the affected local runtime/test path and does not require external services.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): native JS string.slice can cut a surrogate pair, e.g. a boundary emoji can become a lone high surrogate.

## Tests and validation

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/talk/consult-question.test.ts
- Added focused regression coverage for a boundary emoji / surrogate-pair truncation case.
- No known failures from this change.
## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes, malformed truncated text is now avoided while preserving existing caps.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No.
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No.
- What is the highest-risk area? speakable consult result formatting.
- How is that risk mitigated? The change is limited to the existing truncation boundary and covered by focused regression tests.

## Current review state
- Next action: maintainer review and CI.
- Nothing is waiting on the author.
